body:
From Claude:

`set_precipitation_velocities!` builds a closure over `cmc` and `cmp` and broadcasts it, so every quadrature point reads the Chen 2022 coefficient tables out of a runtime struct. The idiom to avoid that is already in this file: #4930 applied it to `set_microphysics_tendency_cache!`, and a third `set_precipitation_velocities!` method does `_fold(dev, cmp), _fold(dev, thp)` itself -- these two methods were simply missed. #4938 then made `Chen2022TerminalVelocity` the default for snow, which is what made the omission expensive.

This applies the same idiom at both `set_precipitation_velocities!` methods, with `_unwrapped` at the six `terminal_velocity` dispatch sites.

## Correction to the original description

This description originally said the change is worth 0.192% of device time and asked that it not be merged expecting SYPD. That was a correct reading of the stack it was measured on, and against current main it is wrong by an order of magnitude, in this PR's own disfavor. Both measurements are below.

## Measured

A100, 120 profiled steps of the coarse AMIP configuration (`amip_coarse_progedmf_1m_land`), Nsight Systems, both arms on the same commit except this change. Measured twice against two different upstream stacks, because the second result is nothing like the first.

### On current main

| kernel | registers/thread | kernel time | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `set_precipitation_velocities` | 115 -> 68 | 2319.8 -> 1659.3 ms | -28.47% |

One fused kernel now, 1200 launches in both arms, 128 threads per block. It saves 660.5 ms over the window, 1.901% of device time, resolved 57.9x over the worst move among 197 paired untreated kernels (11.4 ms).

That is 13.5x the 48.9 ms the same patch saved when it was written. Upstream's 2026-11-03 broadcast fusion merged the two broadcasts this fold targets, 78 and 92 registers, into one set_precipitation_velocities kernel at 115 registers -- above both of them, and past an occupancy step the fold now steps back across. The fold did not change; what it is worth did.

Which makes the figure a property of the current stack rather than of the patch: if the fusion is reverted or the kernel is split, this goes back to being worth about 0.192% of device time, as it was in October.

### End to end

Two independent routes, 0.113 points apart:

| route | SYPD |
| --- | --- |
| the device saving converted through the longwave g-point split, the one treatment whose device saving and SYPD gain are both measured | 1.724% on a steady-state anchor, 1.827% on a full-run one |
| the AMIP pair minus both radiation splits' own in-process measurements, 2.936 - 0.753 - 0.572 | 1.611% |

So roughly 1.6-1.8% of SYPD.

Two things that range does not hide. The residual route is not evidence on its own: 1.611% does not clear the 1.869% floor this stack puts between two *identical* arms, on a 1.196-point spread between the nulls that set that floor. Its value is agreeing with a conversion that is anchored on a treatment which does resolve. And the two anchors differ by 0.103 points, because the conversion divides the longwave's steady-state gain by its device saving while the AMIP pair is a full-run comparison -- a gap the same size as the agreement being claimed, so both are quoted rather than whichever agrees better.

### As written, before the 2026-11-03 fusion

Two kernels then, 1080 launches each:

| broadcast | registers/thread | warps/SM | kernel time | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| environment velocity | 78 -> 48 | 24 -> 40 | 185.9 -> 157.2 ms | -15.47% |
| updraft velocity | 92 -> 56 | 20 -> 36 | 125.1 -> 104.9 ms | -16.08% |

Both cross an occupancy step. Together they saved 48.9 ms over the window, -15.71% of the work they do, and that did not resolve end to end: the AMIP pair read 1.928% against the same 1.869% floor, a margin of 0.059 points. The patch is unchanged since; the inventory it runs on is not.

## Correctness

Only the four members the dispatch reads are folded, as `(; cmc.liquid, cmc.ice, cmc.stokes, cmc.Ch2022)`, rather than `cmc` whole -- a type parameter has to be isbits and `cmc` also carries the aerosol-ML coefficients and the activation parameters. `_unwrapped(p) = p` is the identity on anything not wrapped, so the `set_precipitation_velocities!` methods that do not fold reach the same dispatch unchanged.

The fold changes how the coefficients reach the kernel, not what they are, so I would expect results to be unchanged -- but I have not run a bit-for-bit comparison, and constant folding can change instruction selection, so that is worth checking before merge rather than taking from me.

No NEWS entry, following #4930.

## Reproducing

`exp/2026-10-31-sedimentation-velocity-fold` in the profiling repository this came from carries the as-written measurement: both arms' refs, both Nsight database hashes and the derived figures. The current-main figures are `results/fold-on-current-stack.json`, recorded at `e6fecc6`, from baseline `6c57ba6` and mod `9eb34e3`.
